deep.reconstruction:
WHAT THE PAGE DOES. It is a fair copy, with corrections, of the computation begun on the previous page. Complex numbers are handled in polar form: a 7-place common logarithm of the modulus (characteristic +10, with 'n' marking a negative quantity) plus an argument in degrees, minutes and seconds. There are four 'columns' k = I, II, III, IV, each with complex coefficients a_k, b_k. Riemann writes a', b' for k = I, a'', b'' for II, and so on. Everything is normalised by column I.

(1) Data in polar form. For each column he gives r_k = b'/b_k and s_k = a_k b'/(b_k a').
- Column I: both are 1.
- Column II: log r = 9.9998758, arg 180°7'5.5". log s = 0.7649230, arg 180°12'19.5".
- Column III: log r = 0.0002978, arg 44°55'23.5". log s = 0.3423184 (the transcription reads 0.3423784), arg 92°29'49.5".
- Column IV: log r = 0.0001694, arg 315°22'49.5". log s = 0.4146922, arg 272°13'42.5".

(2) Conversion to Cartesian form. Riemann adds log sin φ and log cos φ to the log-modulus. On the page each pair is written (log|Im|, log|Re|). This gives:
- r_II = −0.999712 − 0.002062i, s_II = −5.819964 − 0.020866i.
- r_III = 0.708701 + 0.706642i, s_III = −0.095829 + 2.197383i.
- r_IV = 0.712064 − 0.702670i, s_IV = 0.101034 − 2.596352i.

(3) Signed sums.
- α = 1 + r_II − r_III − r_IV = −1.420477 − 0.006034i.
- ω = 1 + s_II − s_III − s_IV = −4.825171 + 0.378103i.

(4) Back to polar form. log|Re|, log|Im| and the argument give |z| through log|z| = log|Re| + log sec φ.
- α: log|Re α| = 0.1524342n, log|Im α| = 7.7806053n, arg 180°14'36.2", log|α| = 0.1524381.
- ω: log|Re ω| = 0.6835128n, log|Im ω| = 9.5776102, arg 175°31'9.4", log|ω| = 0.6848422.
- Riemann first wrote log|ω| = 0.6821834, i.e. 0.6835128 − 0.0013294: he subtracted log sec instead of adding it. He did the same for α (0.1524303). That produced the crossed value log(α/ω) = 9.4702469.
- He corrected both, giving log(a'x) = log(α/ω) = 9.4675959 with arg 4°43'26.8".

(5) Products. log(s_k · a'x) = log s_k + log(a'x), and the arguments add. The written moduli 0.2351699, 9.8125653 and 9.8849391 still contain the old 9.4702469. The arguments 184°55'46.3", 97°13'16.3" and 276°57'9.3" are correct.

(6) Cartesian form of a_k b'x/b_k. The crossed-out block used the old modulus. Every crossed log is exactly 0.0026510 larger than its replacement. The final block uses the corrected moduli:
- k = I: a'x = 0.292495 + 0.024171i.
- k = II: −1.701804 − 0.146779i.
- k = III: −0.081143 + 0.640407i.
- k = IV: 0.092309 − 0.756977i.

(7) Then −b'y_k = b'/b_k − a_k b'x/b_k. This means y_k = (a_k x − 1)/b_k, i.e. a_k x − b_k y_k = 1 (my reading). The results are:
- −b'y' = 0.707505 − 0.024171i.
- −b'y'' = 0.702092 + 0.144717i.
- −b'y''' = 0.789844 + 0.066235i.
- −b'y^IV = 0.619755 + 0.054307i.

(8) Finally −b'y = 0.704799 + 0.060272i. I verified that this is the arithmetic mean of the four values.

INTERPRETATION (mine). x is chosen so that y' + y'' − y''' − y^IV = 0. Indeed b'Σε_k y_k = a'xω − α = 0, and that is exactly the definition x = α/(a'ω). With the computed numbers the signed sum of the −b'y_k is about (−2 + 4i)·10^−6. The common value y is then taken as the mean, (y'+y''+y'''+y^IV)/4 = (y'+y'')/2.

The page is a numerical solution of a small complex linear compatibility problem. Its geometric or analytic purpose cannot be determined from this page and its predecessor alone.
errors: Table-interpolation slip in column III. With log|r_III| = 0.0002978 and arg 44°55'23.5", log cos should give log Re = 9.8503642, so Re r_III = 0.708540. Riemann has 9.8504631, i.e. 0.708701. This matches interpolating log cos from 44°55' in the wrong direction (9.8501158 + 0.0000494 + 0.0002978). The imaginary part (9.8491995, 0.706642) is consistent. The error of about 1.6·10^−4 propagates into Re α (should be ≈ −1.420316), x and all the y_k.
Riemann's own slip, which he corrected: log sec φ was first subtracted instead of added for both α and ω (0.6821834, 0.1524303). This produced the crossed-out 9.4702469.

The moduli written beside the products, 0.2351699, 9.8125653 and 9.8849391, were not updated: they still use the wrong 9.4702469 (the correct values are 0.2325189, 9.8099143 and 9.8822881). The subsequent Cartesian values do use the corrected moduli, so the final results are unaffected by this.

results.what: Solving for complex x with a'x = α/ω (α, ω signed sums of coefficient ratios) so that y_k = (a_k x − 1)/b_k satisfy y'+y''−y'''−y^IV = 0, with common y taken as the mean
results.modern_name: Numerical solution of a small complex linear system / compatibility condition

results.what: Complex arithmetic by logarithms: converting between polar form (log modulus, argument) and Cartesian form using log sin, log cos and log sec
results.modern_name: Logarithmic computation with complex numbers in polar form
results.usually_credited_to: standard 18th–19th c. computing practice (Gauss et al.)

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely routine logarithmic numerical computation with complex numbers. It contains no new mathematical idea, and its purpose cannot be identified from this page.
